title: Why Carbon Forms Millions of Compounds
subject: Chemistry
chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
objective: Over 100 elements, yet most known compounds contain carbon. Four reasons, and why silicon can't do the same.

fill.q: A carbon atom forms ____ covalent bonds.
Si–Si bonds are ____ than C–C bonds.
Compounds with the same atoms in a different arrangement are ____.

tf.q: Carbon can form single, double and triple bonds.
Long silicon chains are as stable as carbon chains.
Carbon bonds easily to oxygen and nitrogen.

ar.a: Silicon forms far fewer chain compounds than carbon.

mcq.q: Carbon compounds are so many mainly because of:
C₄H₁₀ has how many structural isomers?
The C–C bond energy is about:
Which is NOT a reason for many carbon compounds?

num.q: How many C–H bonds are in C₄H₁₀?
How many C–C bonds are in a straight chain of 5 carbons?

short.q: Give the four reasons why carbon forms so many compounds.
short.solution: Four bonds, strong C–C bonds, single, double and triple bonds with many partners, and isomerism.

match.explain: Each formula matches its isomer count.
